en.title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
en.author: Fanny J. Crosby
stanzas:
[G]Pass me not, O gentle [D7]Savior,
Hear my humble [G]cry;
[G]While on others Thou art [C]calling,
Do not [D7]pass me [G]by.

Let me at Thy throne of mercy
Find a sweet relief;
Kneeling there in deep contrition,
Help my unbelief.

Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face;
Heal my wounded, broken spirit,
Save me by Thy grace.

Thou the spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me,
Whom have I on earth beside Thee,
Whom in Heav'n but Thee.
en.chorus:
[G]Savior, [D7]Savior,
Hear my humble [G]cry;
[G]While on others Thou art [C]calling,
Do not [D7]pass me [G]by.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths: Crosby's four stanzas and the refrain. The earlier caveat here — that hymnary's bot shield blocked the full page, leaving the wording resting on Timeless Truths alone — is now RESOLVED. Cross-checked 2026-08-01 against gccsatx.com, an independent site, which prints the same four stanzas and the refrain word-for-word with this file. Punctuation and casing differ in stanza 4 between printings: several sources give "Thou the Spring of all my comfort" (capital S) and end the last two lines with question marks, "Whom have I on earth beside Thee? Whom in heav'n but Thee?". This file follows Timeless Truths exactly — lowercase "spring", comma then full stop — which was re-verified against that page rather than assumed. The refrain's last two lines repeat the stanza's melody, so they carry the same chords. Key: the Timeless Truths score is A-flat; G and A are both one semitone away and FORMAT.md's preference order picks G.
